title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

searches.query: "RBAC" interview multi tenant role explosion revocation
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: NIST CSRC: Role-Based Access Control
sources.supportRationale: Original RBAC model and historical standards references for assignment, permissions, hierarchies and separation of duties; no latest-standard claim.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Least privilege, default denial and resource/action authorization on every request, with trusted enforcement and failure handling.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-162: ABAC Definition and Considerations
sources.supportRationale: Subject/object/action/environment attributes evaluated against policy; attribute provenance, policy combining and implementation assumptions are explicit design obligations.

sources.title: IETF RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
sources.supportRationale: Algorithm verification, trusted keys, issuer/audience and distinct JWT usage profiles; not a universal authorization or revocation protocol.

scenarios.theme: An admin in tenant A edits tenant B. What must change?
scenarios.assumptions: The API trusts a role claim but does not resolve its tenant assignment. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to tenant role.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: An admin in tenant A edits tenant B. What must change?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Bind trusted role assignment to the requested resource’s authoritative tenant and enforce action permission at the owner, including batch/admin paths.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Scoped administration adds data checks

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A legitimate cross-tenant support capability needs a separate explicit limited policy rather than accidental global admin text.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to rbac, authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A refund approver approves their own refund. Which check is missing?
scenarios.assumptions: The business requires two distinct people for this workflow. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to self approval.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A refund approver approves their own refund. Which check is missing?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Enforce the relevant separation-of-duties constraint against the request’s trusted initiator and approving actor at the supported action boundary.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Additional workflow state and coordination cost time

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Splitting role names helps administration but cannot alone prove two different actors performed the steps.

scenarios.theme: Every project/status combination needs a new role. Should you keep adding them?
scenarios.assumptions: Administrators can no longer explain effective permissions reliably. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to role explosion.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Every project/status combination needs a new role. Should you keep adding them?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Retain stable job permission bundles and model project/status constraints through an explicit contextual or relationship policy with tested combining behav

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A hybrid adds evaluation inputs and tests

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Pure RBAC remains simpler where duties are stable and context truly does not change permission.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to rbac, abac; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Role removal takes hours to affect exports. What is the policy?
scenarios.assumptions: The promised revocation window is shorter than cached token/role data lifetime. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to revoked cache.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Role removal takes hours to affect exports. What is the policy?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Align invalidation/version/current checks with the required export authorization boundary and test stale/queued requests after removal.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Fresh checks add latency and dependency coupling

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Short cache TTL reduces but does not equal immediate revocation; document the actual window.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz, jwt; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A user grants themselves editor through a hidden endpoint. Where is the defect?
scenarios.assumptions: Read/edit enforcement is correct but the assignment API lacks protected administration policy. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to assignment api.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A user grants themselves editor through a hidden endpoint. Where is the defect?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Authorize role-management actions separately, validate permitted assignment scope and audit changes, then reconcile unauthorized grants and downstream effe

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Administration policy adds controls and support work

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Hiding the button or endpoint from documentation does not protect a callable privileged transition.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz, rbac; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: The role service returns an unfamiliar role after deployment. Should the API allow access?
scenarios.assumptions: A required private action has no recognized permission mapping. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to unknown role.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The role service returns an unfamiliar role after deployment. Should the API allow access?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Deny that action under the default-deny policy, expose safe diagnostics and fix the versioned mapping/rollout before granting it deliberately.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Denying can disrupt legitimate new roles

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A coordinated staged rollout is an alternative; a wildcard allow fallback silently grants undefined authority.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz, rbac; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

publicDisclosure: Researched 2026-11-17. These are adapted production scenarios informed by concept-specific interview searches and the named references below. The System Design Primer provides core orientation where applicable; technical guarantees use the mapped primary sources. Exact interview frequency, rankings and company attribution were not independently verified. Security protocol and runtime examples state their assumptions; the questions test reasoning rather than a universal product recommendation.
